blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text:
Degeneration of dopamine-releasing neurons produces the muscle tremors of Parkinson’s disease.
Insufficient activity of serotonin-releasing neurons may cause depression. Many antidepressant drugs block the elimination of serotonin from the synaptic cleft. So, serotonin remains in the synaptic cleft and reduces depression.

items: Norepinephrine is made in CNS and sympathetic nerves. It regulates sleep patterns, focus and alertness.
Epinephrine is released in adrenal glands and the brainstem. It plays a role in sleep. It also enables to become and stay alert.
Dopamine is a neurotransmitter in brain. It controls body movements, pleasures related to motivation and also emotional stimulation.
Serotonin is produced by the neurons in intestine (approximately 90%), and CNS (10%). It regulates appetite, sleep, memory and learning, temperature, mood, behaviour, muscle contraction etc.
book_errors: produced by the neurons in intestine (approximately 90%)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: About 90% of the body's serotonin is made in the intestine, but by enterochromaffin cells of its lining, not by neurons. The rest is made by neurons, including those of the CNS.
